about: Stage 5 room demo (not a formal result; Ethan chose option A on 2026-10-31): the frozen YOLO and brain in a 4.4 x 4.4 m room with furniture, 12 toys (2 of each target, 3 of each distractor), one continuous run delivering several targets. Deep-merged over the frozen configs: 'stage1' over configs/control/stage1.json, 'stage3' over configs/control/stage3.json (dicts merge, lists and numbers replace). The brain walks the 3 x 3 m field (arena.half_size_m 1.5); the walls stand at room_half_m 2.2 and the furniture sits in the band between, so routes (route.keep_in_m from the field edge) never reach it. Floor: the light-wood floor the detector was trained on. No furniture is red, yellow or green (the colours of the toys) or dark grey (the tray's colour: the frozen YOLO took a dark grey TV stand for the tray, 41 of 216 frames, cloud check 2026-10-31). No shadows (cast_shadows false): the light's shadow map striped the floor and YOLO saw buses in the stripes.

tray.note: on the +x side of the field, 0.2 m between the tray edge and the field edge (as the Stage 1 tray to its wall)
tray.note_round: fix2 2026-10-31 (Ethan: make the tray a round basket): round, 0.3 m across, the Stage 1 tray's 1 cm rim (6 mm thick) and dark grey; together with demo.drop_sides and stage3.drop.d_m it fixes the bounce-out of Ethan's board run (seed 5000: the ketchup, dropped on the side where the bus and henry already lay, bounced off them and out). Why not a taller wall: the toy is released 5-9 cm ahead of the trunk and the toes are 3.4 cm ahead (+1-2.5 cm swing), and the drop walk coasts 4-6 cm, so at the drop the toes reach the rim; the robot steps on a 1 cm rim without trouble (Stage 3E: 11 of 26 drops touched it, 0 falls) but tripped over a 5 cm wall in 2 of 3 drops and over a 2 cm wall in its first drop (cloud seed 5000). Why not wider: at 0.36 m the toes cross the rim while still walking and the robot lurched 14-19 cm into the tray in 2 of 3 drops (cloud seed 5001). The frozen YOLO boxes the round tray as tray (cloud check: 90 of 90 staging views with a 1, 2 or 5 cm wall, 0.3 or 0.36 m, conf about 0.96); the brain measures it with the round rule (stage3/tray.py measure_tray shape 'round'; lateral error rms 0.4 cm against 1.3-3.1 cm with the square rule).

route.note_v2: v2: a route that starts inside the tray's clearance box (tray half + tray_inflate_m, 0.25 m) first steps straight away from the tray centre to tray_exit_m outside that box, then goes round the tray (world.plan_route). Before v2 such a start left the tray out of the route altogether (meant for leaving the spot one stands on): board run 20261112T025144Z, the ketchup's GOTO started 0.19 m from the centre after the henry drop and walked across the tray (0.05 m from the centre at 116.6 s), the bus went out. 0 (stage3.json) keeps the old rule.

drop.note_demo: fix2: the round tray has no corners, so the drop aims 2 cm deeper than Stage 3's 0.21 (the toy is released 5-9 cm ahead of the trunk; cloud, 0.21: 8 of 9 delivered, the miss a ketchup that came down on the rim and slid out; 0.19: 12 of 12 over seeds 5000-5003, 0 falls). 0.19 is also in the Stage 3C sweep (stage3_facts tray_3c c_drop: 9/9, 0 falls, 7 rim touches; 0.21 9/9, 3 touches): the toes reach the 1 cm rim more often, which costs nothing.
drop.note_v2: v2 (Ethan 2026-11-12: walk into the tray and drop at its centre): d_m 0.11, so the toy (at the beak opening 6.8-10.9 cm ahead of the trunk, median 9.4, and up to 3.6 cm to the side; truth.csv, 15 drops) comes down within about 4-5 cm of the centre and a toy that lands on one already there has about 11 cm to the rim instead of about 5 (with one drop side, fix2 0.19 would put every toy about 9 cm out on the same side). Board runs 20261112T02*: the robot went into the tray 6 times by accident (trunk 6.0-13.3 cm from the centre); standing still at the opening (<= 5 cm/s, 3 times) the toy landed 4.3, 8.0 and 6.6 cm from the centre, moving (12.6-23.3 cm/s, 3 times) 12.2, 16.0 and 17.6 cm (2 out): drop.staged makes it creep in and stand still first. 0 falls on those 6 entries; unmeasured: stepping over the rim at creep speed with toys in the tray, and backing out over it (drop.leave). Set 0.19 for fix2's drop outside the rim.

staged.note_v3: v3 (brain.staged_act / staged_drop / drop_not_ready): the beak opens only in the window (d_m - deep_tol_m .. d_m + far_tol_m, centre within aim_open_deg) and standing still (a settle that timed out is a 'wait'); creep only with the centre within aim_open_deg; a retreat moves away from the centre (B10 while it is ahead, pulse_long F5 once it is behind: brain.away). Out of steps or retreats short of the window: result out_of_steps / out_of_retreats, the beak stays shut, back out (back_out) to redo_back_m (carry.staging_m: the tray is seen whole from there) facing the tray, TRAY_LOOK again (re-anchors the odometry on the tray) and DROP from the start, at most max_redos times; then give up: back out the same way, let the toy go there and end drop_fail. Why (v2 validation, runs/20261112T034551Z_s5_v2_validation, 0.11): open_out_of_steps in 4 of 64 Mac and 5 of 69 board drop_step decisions; Mac seed 5000 ketchup opened 23 cm from the centre with it 133 deg off (truth) and missed, after two F2 creeps with the centre about 125 deg off and a B10 'retreat' with it 122 deg off (behind: towards it); board seed 5002 ketchup opened 7 cm from the centre with it 103 deg off and missed (out at 0.23 s). max_redos 1 and redo_back_m are not measured on the new path: about 10 s to back out and 3 s to look again, against the longest v2 target of 99.7 s in episode.max_s 240.
staged.note: v2 (brain.staged_drop):the blind walk to d_m and a fixed stand_s before the beak opens is replaced by: walk to standoff_m from the measured centre, then repeat {settle (drop.settle) -> range r and bearing from odometry since the tray look -> act} until it opens. Acts: r < d_m - deep_tol_m: back off (inching.retreat, B10 about 10.5 cm); r > d_m + far_tol_m: turn to the centre if it is more than aim_turn_deg off and r >= turn_above_m (toes off the rim: no turning with a foot on it or in the tray), else creep with pulse_long (F5, 5.3 cm) or, within long_above_m, pulse_short (F2, 2.1 cm) (stage1_facts pulses_mac); in the window but more than aim_open_deg off: back off and come in again (no turning with a foot on the rim); else open. At most max_steps acts and max_retreats back-offs, then (v2) it opened where it was; v3 does not (note_v3). Why (board runs 20261112T02*, 12 drops recomputed from truth.csv): the walk always stopped where planned (trunk 22.0-23.8 cm from the centre at the stop command, 11 of 12; the 12th was a tray look ranged 7.6 cm long), but in the 1 s stand that followed the robot went on 2.9-14.8 cm (6 of 12 over 8 cm) and turned 1.6-32.6 deg (7 of 12 over 10 deg): the coast from 0.3 m/s carried a foot onto the rim (tray_contact, both feet off the floor) and the policy stepped on into the tray, opening 6.0-13.3 cm from the centre; Mac fix2 run: 2.2-3.8 cm and 3.8-8.3 deg. Odometry saw all of it (walk and stand within about 1 cm and 0.1 deg of truth), so the brain can check before it opens. standoff_m: the toes are about 6 cm ahead of the trunk (3.4 cm + swing), so at 0.25 they stay about 3 cm off the rim (outer edge 0.156 m) while the walk coasts. d_m is where the beak opens (note_v2).

settle.note: v2 (brain.settle): standing still = over the last window_s of robot.state the odometry moved at most still_mps and turned at most still_degps; waited at least min_s, at most max_s (then it goes on and logs still=false). Replaces drop.stand_s in the staged drop (stage0_facts stop_from_0.3mps_mac: 0.7-1.0 s to settle on the floor; on the rim it did not, above).

leave.note_v3: v3 (brain.back_out, used by leave_tray and the staged drop's redo / give-up): every step settles and reads range and bearing; before a pulse the centre must be within aim_back_deg of straight ahead, else turn to face it, but only with the toes off the rim (r >= drop.staged.turn_above_m) and at most max_turns times; the pulse goes away from the centre (B10 while it is ahead, F5 once it is behind); max_no_gain pulses that each gained < min_gain_m of range, or max_pulses pulses (4 -> 6: from 0.11 m to redo_back_m 0.45 takes 4-5 B10 at 10.5 cm), end it not clear (result no_gain / out_of_pulses), and then leave_tray does NOT turn to face_xy (v2 did). Each step is logged (back_step, with its settle result and range gain). Why (v2 validation, runs/20261112T034551Z_s5_v2_validation, truth.csv): board seed 5000 ketchup backed off with the centre 73 deg to the side; on the first pulse a foot caught the rim (left foot on the floor, the other on the tray, wz 5.7 rad/s) and over 4 pulses the robot spun about 210 deg (yaw -16 deg on through 180 to -164), ending 13-15 cm from the centre, then turned there; board seed 5001 henry (opened 2 cm from the centre, aimed) was 23 deg off after two pulses, then a foot caught the rim the same way, it spun about 210 deg and ended about 20-21 cm out; Mac seed 5000 ketchup backed off with the centre 133 deg off (behind), walked into the tray and fell. aim_back_deg, min_gain_m and max_no_gain are not measured: B10 turns 9.4 deg on the floor (2-19; stage1_facts pulses_mac), so aim_back_deg 25 allows about two pulses between turns; a B10 is 10.5 cm, so less than 2 cm is stuck.
leave.note: v2 (brain.leave_tray,Ethan 2026-11-12: back off two steps and turn round after the drop): after the beak closes, back off with inching.retreat (B10, about 10.5 cm) until the trunk is clear_m from the tray centre (from 0.11 m: three pulses; at most max_pulses), then turn to face face_xy (the field centre) if more than turn_tol_deg off. clear_m 0.38 is outside the tray's clearance box (half 0.25 m, corner 0.354 m), so the next target's route goes round the tray. A fall on the way out ends the drop as dropped (the toy is already out of the beak); the next run's brain gets up. Why: board run 20261112T025527Z, the henry drop left the robot standing in the tray (trunk 0.10 m from the centre) and the next run's walk out of it fell and kicked the bus out (160.9 s).

demo.note: toys inside |x|, |y| <= toy_field_m (0.3 m inside the field edge), >= toy_gap_m apart, >= tray_clear_m from the tray centre, >= start_clear_m from the robot start; one layout per seed
demo.note_sides_v2: v2 (Ethan 2026-11-12): no drop_sides any more. fix2 gave each target its own side (x-, y+, y-, brain --side); v2 lets the brain pick the side by the Stage 3 rule (stage3/tray.py choose_side: the shortest route whose lane holds no known toy), as in the formal Stage 4 runs. Expect most drops from x- (10 of 13 cloud drops in fix2's check), so the toys can land near each other: the demo judge counts a toy that leaves the tray under a later drop as knocked_out. demo.py still takes drop_sides if they are put back.
